goal: Run a provider-free deterministic acceptance of CGKN partial repair orchestration without changing benchmark or production gates.
acceptance_criteria: Replay payloads enter only at the Provider HTTP transport boundary and traverse the normal parser and single schema-repair contract.
Actual local CSV and board behaviors determine issue-level acceptance and new-blocker rejection.
Candidate V0 to V1 to V2 advances only on accepted improvements; rejected V3 cannot replace V2.
Accounting and network guards prove zero external Provider calls and exact replay-call accounting.
The report preserves the live-product and live-Provider limitations.

quality_metrics.measure: deterministic scenario coverage and external-network isolation
quality_metrics.target: 8/8 scenarios, real Provider calls=0, accounting consistent, provider_schedulers=1
quality_metrics.method: transport-boundary replay, executable local fixtures, focused regression, rule guard, and kernel contract

prevention: Reuse the existing parser, schema repair, candidate materializer, acceptance helper, accounting writer, and candidate store.
assurance: Hash every replay response and fail immediately on any real network attempt.
control: Execute eight deterministic scenarios, CASE01/CASE03 local behavior checks, focused pytest, guards, and py_compile.
improvement: Apply EXP-CGKN-QUALITY-001 by keeping local logic evidence separate from live product and Provider truth.

interface_expectations: The replay harness is test/evaluation support and is not a Provider scheduler or generation route.
Only scripts.check_connectivity._post_json is replaced for replay responses.
Benchmark cases, evaluator, thresholds, final gate, and candidate product inputs remain unchanged.

feedback: Eight of eight deterministic scenarios passed with zero real network calls and eleven auditable replay transport responses.

CASE01 verified upload, clean, preview, and export while delivery intentionally remained failing; CASE03 verified startup, CRUD, persistence, and export while move intentionally remained failing in the selected candidate.
This evidence validates local orchestration contracts only and does not verify live product repair or Provider repeatability.

worked: Transport-boundary replay exercised the normal Provider response parser and exactly-one schema repair limit.
Actual file, subprocess, reload, CSV, and JSON checks prevented replay declarations from becoming acceptance evidence.
The immutable candidate store kept accepted V2 after a rejected V3.
did_not_work: The first fixture used a package import that was invalid when the entry script ran directly; the fixture was corrected without changing production logic.
The first advisory-score fixture mapped its issue to the wrong file; the fixture mapping was corrected and regression-locked.
experiments: When Provider quota is available, rerun fresh live product convergence; do not promote provider-free logic evidence into live acceptance.
